protocol: ZeroMQ REP request/response with MessagePack payloads (per official LADDER examples/policy_server.py)

transport.framing: one MessagePack request per call; one MessagePack response per call

request.observations: array of one or more independent environment observations

response.actions: same-length array of policy actions in request observation order

observation.images: map camera_name -> HxWx3 uint8 RGB array
observation.eef_pose: 4x4 absolute end-effector transform in robot base frame; metres
observation.joints: array of joint positions in radians
observation.env: environment identity; policy must keep state isolated by this key
observation.first: boolean; true at episode start, reset only this environment's recurrent state

action.pose: 4x4 absolute end-effector transform in robot base frame; metres

optional_chunk.semantics: one action is applied per future control step

invariants: Response action count must equal request observation count.
State must be keyed by env; never share task state across simultaneously active environments.
Reset only the current environment state when observations[].first is true.
Never infer or fabricate privileged simulator state; only use fields exposed by the standard observation contract.
Action poses must be finite, valid transforms in metres and the declared robot base frame.
If perception/planning is indeterminate, return a documented safe/no-op action or fail closed; do not emit a guessed task-completion event.
Official episode success is still decided by LADDER's evaluator, not by the policy-server adapter.

rust_first_architecture.core: Symtropy Rust process owns planning, capability constraints, state, uncertainty and evidence decisions.
rust_first_architecture.adapter: A thin ZeroMQ/MessagePack bridge maps LADDER observations to versioned Rust request structs and returns actions. It may be implemented in Rust; if an official example shim is used, it remains transport-only and outside the Symtropy core.
rust_first_architecture.receipts: Luminous extension receipts are stored separately from official LADDER episode logs and never used to relabel official success.
